messages:
Mira: Heads-up — customer reported promo credits applied but still got charged on invoice. They say dashboard shows 50 free credits remaining, invoice line item shows 0 and there was a ~$12 charge. Org: org_87b9.

billing-bot: Invoice INV-202-87B9 created at 2025-11-02T00:00:01Z. Promo code 'NOV_STANDUP_50' attached.

Samir: Thanks, Mira. Can you paste the sample request id(s) and the exact timestamps the customer used the API?

Mira: They supplied two example requests: req_01: 2025-11-01T23:59:50-05:00 -> generation 320 tokens; req_02: 2025-11-02T00:00:10-05:00 -> generation 410 tokens. Both reported as successful. Customer screenshot of dashboard: shows 50 available credits. Invoice shows credits applied = 0.

Mira: I'm attaching the meter log lines (redacted):
```
2025-11-01T23:59:51Z meter: org=org_87b9 req=req_01 tokens=320 burn_source=free_pool promo_id=promo_554
2025-11-02T00:00:11Z meter: org=org_87b9 req=req_02 tokens=410 burn_source=paid_balance
```

Nora: Interesting — meter shows first req burned promo, second burned paid. But invoice generation job runs at 2025-11-02T00:00:00Z. If invoice snapshot happened between ledger write and promo expiry evaluation, it's possible the invoice saw zero promo balance.

Samir: Do we have promo expiry timestamps for NOV_STANDUP_50?

Mira: Promo meta: created=2025-10-01T00:00:00Z, expires=2025-11-02T00:00:00Z (expires at midnight UTC). Promo TTL in ledger stored as "expires_at=2025-11-02T00:00:00Z".

Nora: That matches a boundary case. Customer's second request at 00:00:10-05:00 equals 2025-11-02T05:00:10Z — after expiry. But invoice snapshot at 00:00:00Z UTC runs before those local times. The mismatch here is that the invoice job queries redeemed credits based on invoice-time snapshot but our metering service reconciles burn_source asynchronously. If a burn event writes after the invoice snapshot but with a timestamp that rounds to the previous day due to local-to-UTC conversion, invoice logic might miss it.

Samir: Can you show the SQL we used to compute promo_remaining at invoice time?

Mira: Query: `SELECT sum(remaining) FROM promo_ledgers WHERE org_id='org_87b9' AND effective_at <= '2025-11-02T00:00:00Z'` — we were using `effective_at <= invoice_time` and ledger writes flush with server-side timestamp. There's a race where meter writes with event_time (customer local) but DB `effective_at` is assigned by ingestion consumer after the invoice snapshot starts.

Nora: Root cause hypothesis: invoice snapshot is taking a view before some ingestion consumers have committed their journaling entries, so applied promo usage that finished exactly at the expiry boundary is missing. That leads to invoice showing no promo applied while later meter lines show promo burns.

EngOps: I can reproduce locally using a timed ingest test: create promo expires=00:00Z, send requests at 23:59:58Z and 00:00:02Z, run invoice snapshot at 00:00:00Z and confirm the 23:59:58 burn arrives after snapshot due to delayed ingestion.

Samir: Action items: (1) refund the customer for the charged tokens and restore 50 promo credits if needed, (2) backfill invoice so charges reflect the burned promo credits, (3) patch invoice job to use stronger consistency (snapshot + wait-for-ingest marker) or compute promo usage from finalized ledger table with commit-time ordering, (4) add test for expiry-boundary cases.

Mira: Customer-facing update: "We're sorry — looks like your promo was applied to earlier usage but an ingestion timing issue caused the invoice to miss it. We're issuing a refund and will backfill the invoice. Will follow up when done." :thumbsup:

Nora: Internal: created INF-2345 to track the backend fix (invoice snapshot ordering + ingest watermark). Assigned to EngOps and Billing.

EngOps: Patch ready, will deploy a small delay+watermark check to invoice job to ensure all ingests up to invoice_time are committed. ETA for deploy: 2025-11-03 18:00Z. After deploy we'll run a backfill script to reconcile invoices for any orgs with promos expiring on snapshot boundaries.

Samir: I'll coordinate the refund and confirm with finance. Mira — can you reply to the customer with the refund ETA and include INV-202-87B9 and INF-2345?

Mira: On it. Reply sent: "Thanks — we've issued a refund and are backfilling the invoice. Reference INF-2345 for the engineering fix and INV-202-87B9 for your billing. Expect refund within 3–5 business days."

EngOps: Postmortem note: add metrics for "invoice snapshot vs last-ingest-commit" to alert if lag > 2s around snapshot times.

Mira: Closing loop here after billing confirms refund. Will update thread when invoice backfill completes.

billing-bot: Billing adjustment REF-987 issued for INV-202-87B9 amount $12.00 — status: pending.
